questions.a: IaC for a data platform templates: resource groups, storage accounts (containers, lifecycle, network rules), Key Vaults and access, ADF/Databricks workspaces, Unity Catalog/metastore bindings, private endpoints/DNS, Log Analytics and diagnostics, RBAC assignments. Environments differ only by parameter files; humans stop clicking resources into existence.

questions.q: What are resource groups, subscriptions, and management groups — how do you organize a data estate?
questions.a: Hierarchy: management groups apply policy/RBAC across subscriptions; subscriptions are billing/isolation boundaries (commonly per environment: dev/test/prod); resource groups bundle same-lifecycle resources (a data platform's storage+ADF+Databricks per environment). Governance (Azure Policy, cost, access) inherits downward — structure it before sprawl.

questions.q: How do you implement cost management: budgets, tags, Azure Advisor, reserved capacity/savings plans?
questions.a: Cost management: tag everything (team, project, environment) for attribution; budgets with alerts per subscription/RG; Azure Advisor recommendations; reservations/savings plans for steady compute; storage lifecycle policies; periodic reviews of orphaned resources (unattached disks, idle clusters, forgotten test environments) — the cheapest workload is the one you deleted.

questions.q: What networking issue commonly breaks self-hosted IR or Databricks-to-source connectivity, and how do you debug it?
questions.a: Common connectivity break: private networking — SHIR VM can't reach the source (NSG/firewall rules, DNS not resolving private endpoints, proxy interference) or Databricks can't reach storage (missing private endpoint approval, wrong DNS zone). Debug: test name resolution and port connectivity from the compute (nslookup, Test-NetConnection), check effective NSG rules, private endpoint approvals, and firewall logs — it's almost always DNS or an NSG.

questions.q: How do you copy on-premises SQL Server data to ADLS securely — walk through components and auth end to end.
questions.a: On-prem SQL → ADLS securely: install self-hosted IR on a server with line-of-sight to SQL (outbound 443 only); linked service authenticates via Key Vault-stored credentials (or Windows auth); copy activity writes Parquet to ADLS via managed identity/service principal with Storage Blob Data Contributor scoped to the landing container; storage locked to private endpoints/firewall; watermark table drives incrementals; diagnostics to Log Analytics.

questions.q: What is Azure Container Registry / AKS at a high level, and when do data teams touch containers?
questions.a: ACR stores container images; AKS runs them at scale. Data teams touch containers for: custom Airflow/Prefect deployments, containerized ingestion apps and APIs, dbt/python job images run on Kubernetes or Container Apps, and packaging dependencies immune to environment drift — increasingly standard even in 'SQL shops'.

questions.q: How do you handle file arrival-based processing in Azure (Event Grid → ADF/Function/Auto Loader)?
questions.a: File-arrival processing options: Event Grid blob-created events triggering ADF event triggers (pipeline per file/batch), an Azure Function for lightweight custom handling, or Databricks Auto Loader in file-notification mode consuming the same events at scale — pick ADF for orchestration-centric flows, Auto Loader for high-volume lakehouse ingestion.

questions.q: What is the medallion architecture on Azure concretely: which services own landing, Bronze, Silver, Gold, and serving?
questions.a: Concrete Azure medallion: sources land via ADF/event triggers into ADLS raw (landing zone, immutable); Databricks/Fabric Spark conforms to Bronze Delta then Silver (dedupe, SCD, quality gates); Gold star schemas built via Spark/dbt/Warehouse; served through Fabric Direct Lake or Databricks SQL to Power BI; Purview/Unity Catalog governing; ADF or Workflows orchestrating; everything deployed via DevOps.

questions.q: What is Azure Entra ID's role in data platform security (groups for RBAC, conditional access, service principals)?
questions.a: Entra ID centralizes identity: security groups (not individuals) receive RBAC and workspace roles, service principals/managed identities for non-human access, conditional access enforcing MFA/compliant devices for sensitive data tools, PIM for time-boxed elevated roles, and audit logs feeding governance — identity is the primary security perimeter in cloud data platforms.

questions.q: How do you implement row-level and column-level security across the Azure SQL/Synapse/Fabric family?
questions.a: RLS: Azure SQL security policies with predicate functions filter rows per user; Fabric Warehouse supports similar T-SQL RLS; semantic-model RLS handles the BI layer. CLS: GRANT column-level permissions, dynamic data masking for casual protection, or OLS in semantic models. Enforce closest to the data consumers actually hit, and align layers so alternate paths don't bypass.

questions.q: What is geo-redundancy vs availability zones, and how do you design a DR strategy for a data platform (RPO/RTO)?
questions.a: Availability zones protect within a region (independent datacenters — HA for zone failure); geo-redundancy protects across regions (paired-region replicas — DR for regional disaster). DR design: define RPO/RTO per tier; GZRS storage plus IaC-rebuildable compute is often enough for analytics (rebuild beats hot standby); business-critical serving gets failover groups/secondary capacity; test the DR runbook annually or it's fiction.

questions.q: How do you migrate an on-prem data warehouse to Azure — assessment, landing zone, migration waves, validation?
questions.a: On-prem DW migration: assess (inventory schemas, ETL, consumers, sizing; classify by complexity); establish landing zone (network, identity, governance, IaC) first; migrate historical data via bulk transfer, then incremental sync (ADF/replication) during transition; convert ETL by pattern not line-by-line; parallel-run with automated reconciliation; migrate consumers in waves; cut over per subject area with rollback windows; decommission with a date.

questions.q: What certifications map to this stack (DP-203/DP-600/DP-700) and what do they cover?
questions.a: Certification map: DP-203 (retiring lineage: Azure data engineering — ADF, Synapse, Databricks, storage), DP-600 (Fabric Analytics Engineer — semantic models, warehouses, lakehouse analytics), DP-700 (Fabric Data Engineer — ingestion, transformation, Spark, RTI, administration in Fabric). For your target roles: DP-600 + DP-700 cover the Microsoft stack authoritatively.

questions.q: How do you benchmark and choose between ADF, Databricks, and Fabric for a new greenfield pipeline in 2026?
questions.a: 2026 decision lens: Fabric — Microsoft-centric org, BI-heavy consumption, SaaS simplicity, capacity licensing suits viewer scale. Databricks — engineering-heavy workloads, streaming/ML depth, multicloud, code-first team. ADF alone — pure movement/orchestration into either. Benchmark with a representative slice (your biggest join, your spikiest concurrency) and evaluate TCO including people-time, not just compute rates.

questions.q: Design an end-to-end Azure architecture for daily + streaming logistics data feeding Power BI, with security, monitoring, and CI/CD.
questions.a: Design: batch sources via ADF (SHIR for on-prem) + streaming via Event Hubs → ADLS/OneLake landing → Databricks or Fabric Spark builds Bronze→Silver→Gold Delta (quality gates, SCD2 dims, charge-line-grain facts) → Direct Lake/SQL warehouse semantic model with RLS → Power BI apps; Eventstream→Eventhouse for live tracking dashboards; Purview + Unity Catalog governance; Key Vault + managed identities + private endpoints security; Log Analytics + capacity metrics monitoring with Teams alerting; DevOps CI/CD deploying IaC, pipelines, and models.

questions.q: A stakeholder reports the nightly ADF load failed and business reports are stale. Walk through your incident response: triage, comms, rerun strategy, and postmortem.
questions.a: Incident response: acknowledge and triage (which pipeline, which activity, error class) via monitoring before stakeholders escalate; communicate impact and ETA to consumers early (stale-data banner beats silent wrongness); fix or bypass root cause (rerun from failed activity for transient issues, hotfix for logic, source escalation for upstream); rerun idempotently and validate freshness/reconciliation before declaring resolved; postmortem: root cause, detection gap (why did users know before alerts?), and prevention actions with owners.
